text:
CHAIN
L1: Delta-parameterised depthwise causal taps (lags 0–3) on the expanded `kv` tensor -> keys and values in some layers pick up previous-token content | quantity: per-layer |tap lag-1| over |identity + tap lag-0| on the key channels | baseline: 0 (identity init) | expect: up; mean |lag-1 tap| of 0.1–0.6 in at least layers 0–3 by step 300, smaller in late layers | breaks if: every lag≥1 tap stays below 0.05 at step 300, or the taps shrink back toward 0 after rising
L2: Previous-token-carrying keys -> one head in an early layer attends to j where x_{j-1}=x_t (a single-layer induction pattern) | quantity: attention entropy in layers 0–3; induction score (attention mass on "token after the previous occurrence of x_t") | baseline: entropy L0 0.957, L1 0.903, L2 0.854, L3 0.804; induction score unmeasured | expect: entropy down 0.05–0.2 in at least one of layers 0–3; induction score up at least 2x vs baseline at matched step | breaks if: entropy and induction score match baseline within seed spread at step 300
L3: Induction pattern -> recall-token loss falls faster | quantity: recall-token loss (13% of targets) | baseline: 4.475 at step 100 (rest 6.704) | expect: below baseline by 0.05–0.3 nats at matched steps from step ~200–300 onward | breaks if: gap is within seed noise at step 1000
L4: Copying from far context -> late positions gain more than early ones | quantity: loss(256–1024) minus loss(0–64) | baseline: +0.459 at step 100 | expect: smaller by 0.05–0.2 at matched step | breaks if: unchanged or larger
L5: Recall gain plus phrase-level key/value matching, with non-recall tokens unharmed -> exam val loss down | quantity: exam val_loss after 1525 steps | baseline: pooled mean unmeasured here | expect: down 0.01–0.04 nats | breaks if: non-recall loss rises enough to cancel, or the net gain is under 0.005 or not significant at 3 seeds
WEAKEST: L2

QUESTIONS
Q1: Does the 2.2-nat recall gap measure induction, or just that bigrams repeated within a window are frequent and easy? | decides: target metric "recall-token loss" vs a frequency-controlled metric (second vs first in-window occurrence of rank>1000 bigrams)
A1: Unknown. The measurement does not control for frequency, and repeated bigrams skew toward common ones, so part of the 4.475 vs 6.704 gap is unigram/bigram statistics. Build the controlled metric. Without it, a move in L3 cannot be attributed to L2.

Q2: Does the baseline form an induction head inside the 1525-step budget anyway? | decides: taps in all 12 layers vs only early layers; also whether the end-of-run gain can persist or only the curve shifts earlier
A2: Unknown for this setup. Olsson et al. saw the phase change at roughly 2.5–5B tokens in their models (https://transformer-circuits.pub/2022/in-context-learning-and-induction-heads/index.html). Muon-trained small models learn far faster, so that number does not transfer. Layer-0 entropy of 0.957 at step 100 shows no sharp positional head yet. If the baseline forms one by step ~300, the conv only buys a head start, and the step-1525 gap may shrink below 0.005.

Q3: Which optimizer group and which parameterisation should the taps get? | decides: raw kernel with identity tap vs delta form (kv + Σ w_l·shift(kv,l), w init 0); Muon vs AdamW
A3: `build_optimizers` sends every 2-D parameter not named tok/head to Muon. A (4,768) tap tensor would get orthogonalised updates scaled by sqrt(768/4)≈13.9 at lr 0.02, which wrecks it. In AdamW, wd 0.1 at lr 3e-3 pulls a raw identity tap down by about e^-0.38≈0.68 over the run when no gradient opposes it. Use the delta form, route it to AdamW explicitly or store it 3-D, and preferably give it wd 0.

Q4: Should the taps go before or after `k_norm`, and do they touch the rotary key? | decides: conv on `kv` before view/k_norm vs on k after k_norm
A4: Put them before, on the contiguous `kv = expand(...)` of shape (B,T,768). k_norm then re-normalises the mixed key, so QK-norm still holds logit scale. A conv after k_norm would change key RMS and the effective 1/sqrt(96) temperature. Leave `kr` (shared 32-dim rope key) and `qr` untouched so position encoding stays per-token.

Q5: Should the taps sit on the 768 expanded channels or on the 128-dim latent? | decides: expanded (36,864 params) vs latent before latent_norm (6,144 params)
A5: Expanded gives independent kernels for key and value channels, per head, so a head can have prev-token keys and current-token values at once. That is the exact induction wiring. The latent version shares each kernel between every k and v channel that reads that latent dim and relies on `expand` to route. Primer puts its depthwise conv after the per-head projections (https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.08668). Both are far under C3, so pick expanded.

Q6: Should it be implemented with `F.conv1d` or with shift-and-add? | decides: conv1d with (B,C,T) transposes vs F.pad shift-add on (B,T,C)
A6: Shift-add on the contiguous (B,T,768) tensor avoids two transposes and copies, and costs three fused-ish elementwise ops per layer. Cast the taps with `.to(kv.dtype)` like the script does for the mixing weights, otherwise fp32 upcasts double the memory of those tensors. The step-time cost is unmeasured. Belief: 1–3% given that the 4-stream mixing already does similar elementwise work.

Q7: Can a recall-only gain pass C7? | decides: kv-only (recall-targeted) vs a broader q/k/v version aimed at all tokens
A7: Overall Δ ≈ 0.13·Δrecall + 0.87·Δrest, so recall tokens alone must improve by ≥0.04 nats just to clear the 0.005 margin. p<0.01 at 3 seeds needs more than that, and seed std is unmeasured. Primer reports MDHA gains in overall LM loss, not only on repeats (https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.08668). L5 therefore depends on phrase-level effects on non-recall tokens too.

Q8: Should the taps also go on queries? | decides: kv-only vs q-content + kv
A8: Induction needs only shifted keys. Primer convolves Q, K and V with kernel 3 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.08668). If q is added, apply it only to the 64 content dims of the 576-wide `wq` output, never to the 32 rope dims. Start with kv-only for clean attribution.

Q9: Can the conv leak future tokens into the exam? | decides: left pad (lags 0..3) vs any centred/right pad; whether a causality test is mandatory
A9: The shift must be `F.pad(kv, (0,0,l,0))[:, :T]`, i.e. position t reads t−l. A reversed shift leaks x_{t+1}, gives a spuriously low loss, and the harness exam would reward it. The builder must check that changing idx[:, t+1] leaves logits[:, :t+1] unchanged. Positions 0–2 see zero padding in both training and exam windows, so the two are consistent.

Q10: Does the 45-step/1000-step test plan match the real schedule? | decides: `--smoke-steps 1000` (schedule compressed, cooldown from step 700) vs the full-run schedule truncated at 1000
A10: `lr_mult` uses `total_steps = smoke_steps`, so a 1000-step smoke run has a different schedule from the 1525-step run (warmup 30, cooldown from 1067). Both arms must use the same steps setting. Recall-loss checkpoints are not logged by the script, so they need a separate probe.

KNOWN
- `kv = expand(latent_norm(compress(x)))` is (B,T,768) and is viewed as (B,T,6,128) per head, then chunked into k(64) and v(64). A per-channel conv on `kv` before the view is equivalent to per-head k/v convs [script]
- q and k are 96 wide (64 content + 32 decoupled rope, one shared rope key head); SDPA default scale is 1/sqrt(96); v is 64 wide [script]
- Taps of lags 0–3 on 768 channels × 12 layers = 36,864 params, about 0.17% of 21.24M non-embedding, well under C3 [script]
- Any 2-D param not named tok/head goes to Muon with lr 0.02 and scale sqrt(max(1,rows/cols)). Taps must be routed to AdamW (3-D shape or explicit filter) [script]
- AdamW group uses lr 3e-3, wd 0.1, betas (0.9,0.95). A delta-form tap initialised to zero makes weight decay pull toward identity, not toward zero [script]
- Training is 1525 steps (50e6 // 32768), 8 micro-batches of 4×1024, warmup 30 steps, cooldown from step 1067, grad clip 1.0 [script]
- The exam calls GPT(cfg).forward(idx) on model.pt, so the taps must be built unconditionally in `Attention.__init__` (or under a Config field defaulting on) so state_dict loads strictly [script]
- Under autocast, cast taps with `.to(x.dtype)` as `combine` does, to avoid fp32 intermediates [script]
- micro_batch 8 already spilled past 6 GB, so VRAM headroom at 4 is limited; extra saved activations are about 4 × 4×1024×768 × 2 B ≈ 25 MB per layer at most [script]
- Recall tokens are 13% of targets, with loss 4.475 vs 6.704 for the rest at step 100 [measured]
- Layer-0 attention entropy is 0.957 (near flat) and first-token attention mass is ≤0.006 everywhere, so there is no sink to fix [measured]
- Layer-0 attention grad norm is about 10x layers 1–11 on 3 seeds (z 7.03) [measured]
- Late-minus-early position loss is +0.459 at step 100, so the model does not yet profit from long context [measured]
- Primer's Multi-DConv-Head Attention adds depthwise kernel-3 convs after the Q, K, V projections and was among its main gains (https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.08668) [web]
- Induction heads formed at roughly 2.5–5B tokens in Olsson et al.'s models; this is setup-specific (https://transformer-circuits.pub/2022/in-context-learning-and-induction-heads/index.html) [web]
- Kernel 4 exceeds the lag 1 that induction needs; lags 2–3 serve phrase matching [belief]
- Step time and peak VRAM of the baseline are not in the measurements, so the "5.0 s" kill threshold cannot be checked against C4 here [measured]

ASSUMES
- Previous-token information is the bottleneck for in-context copying at this budget, not query or value capacity
- The same temporal kernel family is useful in all 12 layers
- Keys and values both benefit from mixing; queries stay single-token
- Temporal mixing belongs inside attention rather than in the residual stream or the MLP
- Learned taps are needed; a fixed shift would not suffice
- Step-0 equality with the baseline (identity init) matters for the outcome
- Every block keeps full-context softmax attention as its sequence mixer

NEW IDEAS

SLOT: drop
IDEA: Parameter-free latent half-shift
MECHANISM: Drop "learned taps are needed". Replace 32 of the 128 compressed-latent channels with their value at t−1 (RWKV-style token shift) before latent_norm. Zero parameters; `expand` learns which keys and values read shifted channels.
PREDICTION: Recall-token loss tracks the learned-conv version within 0.02 nats if lag-1 alone carries the effect.
TEST: 300 matched steps against baseline and against the conv version; compare recall loss and L0–3 entropy.
SOURCE: own
PART: Sequence mixing: head count, head structure and output projection
KIND: port

SLOT: strengthen
IDEA: Input-selected lag mixture per head
MECHANISM: Per head, compute 4 lag weights as softmax(x·W_lag), with W_lag of 384×4 per head, initialised so lag 0 has weight ≈1. Each token then chooses whether its key describes itself, the previous token or a phrase.
PREDICTION: Larger recall gain than static taps, plus lower loss on rank 1000–10000 tokens (multi-token words).
TEST: 300 matched steps; compare loss by frequency bucket against the static-conv run.
SOURCE: own
PART: Sequence mixing: head count, head structure and output projection
KIND: port

SLOT: specialise
IDEA: Taps only in layers 0–2
MECHANISM: Put the delta taps only where keys are built from near-raw embeddings and where the 10x layer-0 grad anomaly sits; layers 3–11 stay unchanged.
PREDICTION: At least 80% of the all-layer recall gain with 9,216 params, and layer-0 attention grad norm closer to its neighbours.
TEST: 300 matched steps, 3 arms (none / 0–2 / all); recall loss and layer-0 grad ratio.
SOURCE: own
PART: Sequence mixing: head count, head structure and output projection
KIND: port

SLOT: port
IDEA: Short causal conv on the SwiGLU input
MECHANISM: Depthwise delta-form kernel-4 causal conv on the normed MLP input (384 channels) before w_gate/w_up, so the MLP computes on local n-grams, not single positions.
PREDICTION: Loss on rank 1000–50304 tokens falls faster (word-piece completion); recall loss is unaffected.
TEST: 300 matched steps; loss by frequency bucket.
SOURCE: own
PART: Feed-forward (SwiGLU MLP)
KIND: port

SLOT: combine
IDEA: kv conv + sparse per-head output gate
MECHANISM: Add the modded-nanoGPT per-head sigmoid gate fed by 12 residual channels on SDPA output before wo. Heads that become induction heads can switch off when there is no earlier repeat, instead of writing a noisy average.
PREDICTION: Non-recall loss no worse than baseline while recall gain is kept; layer-0 attention grad ratio drops below 5x.
TEST: 300 matched steps, 4 arms (2×2); recall vs non-recall loss.
SOURCE: https://www.greaterwrong.com/posts/j3gp8tebQiFJqzBgg/how-the-nanogpt-speedrun-wr-dropped-by-20-in-3-months
PART: Sequence mixing: head count, head structure and output projection
KIND: port

SLOT: other
IDEA: Layer 0 without attention, a pure conv mixer
MECHANISM: Layer-0 attention is near flat (entropy 0.957), so it acts mostly as a running average. Replace layer 0's attention branch with a delta-form kernel-4 depthwise causal conv plus wo, saving about 0.5M params, and keep the conv taps in layers 1–11.
PREDICTION: Matched-step loss within ±0.02 of baseline at step 45, and better from step 300 because layer 0 becomes a dedicated local n-gram builder.
TEST: 45 matched steps, then 300.
SOURCE: own
PART: Sequence mixing: head count, head structure and output projection
KIND: leap
BREAKS: every block's sequence mixer is full-context softmax attention
KILL: mean loss over steps 41–50 more than 0.03 nats above baseline's mean over the same steps

OPEN
- What is the baseline exam val_loss seed std at 1525 steps? | build: yes | decides: 3 seeds vs 5+ seeds; whether a ~0.01 effect is worth building
- Does the baseline form an induction head before step 1525, and at which step? | build: yes | decides: all-layer taps vs early-layer taps; head-start vs persistent-gain framing
- How much of the recall-token gap is frequency rather than copying? | build: yes | decides: recall-loss target vs frequency-controlled repeat metric
- What are the baseline step time and peak VRAM on the 4050? | build: no | decides: whether the 5.0 s kill threshold matches C4's 2x limit
- Should the taps have wd 0 or 0.1 in AdamW, and lr 3e-3 or lower? | build: yes | decides: a separate AdamW param group vs reusing the "other" group
- Does conv on v help or hurt copying fidelity relative to k-only? | build: yes | decides: taps on all 768 kv channels vs only the 384 key channels
- Do the lag-2/3 taps learn anything at this budget, or only lag 1? | build: yes | decides: kernel 4 vs kernel 2
